prompt: One MouseListener watches three buttons. Complete mouseEntered/mouseExited so a status label tracks the hovered button and a late exit from a different button is ignored.
explanation: Enter and exit events arrive per component, so a listener shared by several components must ask e.getComponent() who the event is about. Comparing the exiting component with the currently hovered one is what makes the tracking robust: when the pointer slides from one button to the next, the enter for the new button can arrive before the exit for the old one. Keeping the hovered name in a nullable field, and translating null to "none" in the getter, keeps "nothing hovered" a first-class state.
hints: e.getComponent() returns the component the event happened on -- call getName() on it.
In mouseExited, compare the exiting name with the stored hovered name before clearing anything.
Compare with leaving.equals(hovered) after a null check, not with ==, because these are String objects.
